### Data Formatting
```{python}
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import re

output_path = r"C:\Users\ohdaw\OneDrive - Harvard University\snu_remains\redo\FINAL_dataset_2019only.csv"
data = pd.read_csv(output_path, encoding="utf-8")

group_cols = [c for c in data.columns if re.match(r'^[MW]_\d{4}$', c)]

# Build park variables
data["green_ratio"] = data["greenarea_area"] / data["park_area"] * 100
data["user_area"] = (
      data["openspaace_area"]
    + data["road_area"]
    + data["walkingtrail_area"]
    + data["shadecanopy_area"]
)
data["user_ratio"] = data["user_area"] / data["park_area"] * 100
data["amenity_number"] = (
      data["gymtrack_number"]
    + data["swimmingpool_number"]
    + data["sportsfacility_number"]
    + data["playground_number"]
    + data["cafeteria_number"]
    + data["kiosk_number"]
)
data["parking_number"] = data["parkingcapacity_number"]
data["transit_number"] = data["bus500"] + data["sub500"]
data["park_area_ha"]   = data["park_area"] / 10_000

amenities = ["green_ratio", "user_ratio", "amenity_number",
             "parking_number", "transit_number", "park_area_ha"]

# Wide -> long
data_long = data.melt(
    id_vars=["INFLOW_CD", "ID", "c_eq_min"] + amenities,
    value_vars=group_cols,
    var_name="group",
    value_name="visitors"
)
data_long = data_long[data_long["visitors"] > 0].copy()

# Parse sex & age
def parse_group(g):
    female = 1 if g[0] == "W" else 0
    age_lo = int(g[2:4])
    age_hi = int(g[4:6])
    age_mid = (age_lo + age_hi) / 2
    return female, age_mid

data_long[["female", "age"]] = data_long["group"].apply(
    lambda x: pd.Series(parse_group(x))
)
data_long["age_sq"] = data_long["age"] ** 2

# Center/scale age before interactions -- keeps CCREM better conditioned
data_long["age_c"]    = data_long["age"] - data_long["age"].mean()
data_long["age_c_sq"] = data_long["age_c"] ** 2

for a in amenities:
    data_long[f"{a}_F"]    = data_long[a] * data_long["female"]
    data_long[f"{a}_A"]    = data_long[a] * data_long["age_c"]
    data_long[f"{a}_FA"]   = data_long[a] * data_long["female"] * data_long["age_c"]
    data_long[f"{a}_A2"]   = data_long[a] * data_long["age_c_sq"]
    data_long[f"{a}_FA2"]  = data_long[a] * data_long["female"] * data_long["age_c_sq"]

data_long["ID"] = data_long["ID"].astype(str)
data_long["INFLOW_CD"] = data_long["INFLOW_CD"].astype(str)

export_path = r"C:\Users\ohdaw\OneDrive - Harvard University\snu_remains\redo\data_long_for_ccrem.csv"
data_long.to_csv(export_path, index=False, encoding="utf-8")
print(f"Exported {data_long.shape[0]} rows, {data_long.shape[1]} columns to:\n{export_path}")
```

### CCREM 
```{python}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import os

output_dir = r"C:\Users\ohdaw\OneDrive - Harvard University\snu_remains\redo\var_distributions"
os.makedirs(output_dir, exist_ok=True)

# Core variables feeding the model — raw amenities, demographics, outcome, and weights.
# (Skipping the _F/_A/_FA/_A2/_FA2 interaction columns since they're just products
#  of these — check them here first, and interactions will follow the same pattern.)
vars_to_check = amenities + ["female", "age", "age_c", "age_sq", "age_c_sq",
                              "c_eq_min", "visitors"]

for var in vars_to_check:
    if var not in data_long.columns:
        print(f"Skipping {var} — not found in data_long")
        continue

    plt.figure(figsize=(6, 4))
    plt.hist(data_long[var].dropna(), bins=30, edgecolor="black", alpha=0.75)
    plt.title(f"Distribution of {var}")
    plt.xlabel(var)
    plt.ylabel("Count")
    plt.tight_layout()

    safe_name = var.replace("/", "_")
    plt.savefig(os.path.join(output_dir, f"dist_{safe_name}.png"), dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight")
    plt.show()
    plt.close()

    # Quick numeric summary alongside each plot — helpful for spotting scale mismatches at a glance
    print(f"{var}: min={data_long[var].min():.3f}, max={data_long[var].max():.3f}, "
          f"mean={data_long[var].mean():.3f}, sd={data_long[var].std():.3f}\n")
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

scale_check <- data_long %>%
  select(all_of(vars_to_check)) %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), list(
    min = ~min(., na.rm = TRUE),
    max = ~max(., na.rm = TRUE),
    sd  = ~sd(., na.rm = TRUE)
  ))) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = c("variable", ".value"), names_pattern = "(.*)_(min|max|sd)$") %>%
  arrange(desc(sd))

print(scale_check, n = Inf)
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)
library(performance)
library(car)
library(ggplot2)

# Patch for R < 4.4 where %||% isn't in base -- lme4's summary printing
# uses it internally (via reformulas::format_sdvar), so without this,
# printing/summarizing any lmer model object fails on this R version.
`%||%` <- function(x, y) if (is.null(x)) y else x

data_long <- read.csv(
  "C:/Users/ohdaw/OneDrive - Harvard University/snu_remains/redo/data_long_for_ccrem.csv",
  encoding = "UTF-8"
)

data_long$ID        <- as.factor(data_long$ID)
data_long$INFLOW_CD <- as.factor(data_long$INFLOW_CD)

# Normalize visitor weights to mean 1 -- preserves relative weighting while
# keeping residual variance/R2/AIC on an interpretable scale (raw range was
# 0.01 to 662,707, which distorted variance-based fit statistics)
data_long$visitors_norm <- data_long$visitors / mean(data_long$visitors)

amenities <- c("green_ratio", "user_ratio", "amenity_number",
               "parking_number", "transit_number", "park_area_ha")

# Centered age used throughout to avoid age/age_sq collinearity (VIF was ~200
# with raw age; centering resolves this without changing fitted values)
fixed_vars_sq <- c(
  "female", "age_c", "age_c_sq",
  amenities,
  paste0(amenities, "_F"),
  paste0(amenities, "_A"),
  paste0(amenities, "_FA"),
  paste0(amenities, "_A2"),
  paste0(amenities, "_FA2")
)

formula_str <- as.formula(
  paste("c_eq_min ~", paste(fixed_vars_sq, collapse = " + "),
        "+ (1|ID) + (1|INFLOW_CD)")
)

ccrem_normw_t <- lmerTest::lmer(
  formula_str,
  data = data_long,
  weights = visitors_norm,
  control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5))
)

summary(ccrem_normw_t)
```


### Diagnostic
```{r}
cat("=== isSingular ===\n")
print(isSingular(ccrem_normw_t))

cat("\n=== VarCorr (variance components) ===\n")
print(VarCorr(ccrem_normw_t))

cat("\n=== rePCA (which RE dimension is degenerate) ===\n")
print(summary(rePCA(ccrem_normw_t)))

cat("\n=== ICC by group ===\n")
print(icc(ccrem_normw_t, by_group = TRUE))

cat("\n=== VIF ===\n")
print(vif(ccrem_normw_t))

cat("\n=== R2 ===\n")
print(r2(ccrem_normw_t))

cat("\n=== AIC / BIC / logLik ===\n")
print(AIC(ccrem_normw_t))
print(BIC(ccrem_normw_t))
print(logLik(ccrem_normw_t))
```


### Cross-optimizer Stability Check
```{r}
meth.tab <- cbind(optimizer = c("bobyqa", "Nelder_Mead"), method = c("", ""))

af <- allFit(ccrem_normw_t, meth.tab = meth.tab)

cat("=== Which optimizers converged OK ===\n")
print(summary(af)$which.OK)

cat("\n=== Fixed effects across optimizers (amenity vars) ===\n")
print(summary(af)$fixef[, amenities])

cat("\n=== Log-likelihood across optimizers ===\n")
print(summary(af)$llik)

cat("\n=== Random-effect variance components across optimizers ===\n")
print(summary(af)$sdcor)
```


### Marginal effects by age group and sex
```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

coefs <- fixef(ccrem_normw_t)
age_mean <- mean(data_long$age)   # from the ORIGINAL (uncentered) age column used to build age_c

age_groups <- c(
  "0-9" = 5, "10-19" = 15, "20-29" = 25, "30-39" = 35,
  "40-49" = 45, "50-59" = 55, "60-69" = 65, "70+" = 75
)
age_groups_centered <- age_groups - age_mean

marginal_effect_sq <- function(coefs, var, age_c, female) {
  age_c_sq <- age_c^2
  b    <- coefs[[var]]
  bf   <- coefs[[paste0(var, "_F")]]
  ba   <- coefs[[paste0(var, "_A")]]
  bfa  <- coefs[[paste0(var, "_FA")]]
  ba2  <- coefs[[paste0(var, "_A2")]]
  bfa2 <- coefs[[paste0(var, "_FA2")]]

  b + female*bf + age_c*ba + female*age_c*bfa +
    age_c_sq*ba2 + female*age_c_sq*bfa2
}

marginal_table <- expand.grid(
  Amenity = amenities,
  AgeGroup = names(age_groups),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
) %>%
  mutate(
    AgeCentered = age_groups_centered[AgeGroup],
    Men_Effect   = mapply(marginal_effect_sq, Amenity, AgeCentered, MoreArgs = list(coefs = coefs, female = 0)),
    Women_Effect = mapply(marginal_effect_sq, Amenity, AgeCentered, MoreArgs = list(coefs = coefs, female = 1)),
    W_minus_M    = Women_Effect - Men_Effect
  )

#print(marginal_table, n = Inf)
library(tibble)
print(as_tibble(marginal_table), n = Inf)
```


### Plot
```{r}
library(ggplot2)

age_order <- names(age_groups)
marginal_table$AgeGroup <- factor(marginal_table$AgeGroup, levels = age_order)

marginal_long <- marginal_table %>%
  select(Amenity, AgeGroup, Men_Effect, Women_Effect) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(Men_Effect, Women_Effect), names_to = "Sex", values_to = "Effect") %>%
  mutate(Sex = ifelse(Sex == "Men_Effect", "Men", "Women"))

ggplot(marginal_long, aes(x = AgeGroup, y = Effect, color = Sex, group = Sex)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +
  facet_wrap(~ Amenity, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    title = "Marginal Effect of Park Variables on Travel Cost by Age Group and Sex",
    subtitle = "CCREM, centered age, normalized visitor weights",
    x = "Age Group", y = "Effect on travel cost (min)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

ggsave(
  "C:/Users/ohdaw/OneDrive - Harvard University/snu_remains/redo/marginal_effects_ccrem.png",
  width = 12, height = 7, dpi = 150
)
```
